Player spawns as a purple block, collects small stray blocks to merge into larger squares, tests W to eject blocks and A/D to rotate, and observes white obstacle blocks and the map border.
Player battles and destroys Ashdubhh and great bodl, grows a large central block, and duels Dynobuster YT until colliding with Dynobuster YT's larger core block and dying.
Death overlay displays final score of 247 with Facebook/Twitter share buttons and Continue button.
Player respawns as an orange block, destroys dodoKing and great bod, watches great bodl die to a white obstacle block, and fights a large light-purple player until dying.
Death overlay displays final score of 144; player clicks Continue.

Player spawns as a cyan block, skirmishes with Slogoman and a purple player, receives fed blocks from LOL, scavenges debris from players hitting white obstacles, and kills an orange player to reach #2.
Player encounters #1 player N (giant cyan block), destroys super and smaller players, and is killed when N shoots blocks and rams into him.
Death overlay shows final score of 569 as player wraps up the video.
Highlight clip of Kwebbelkop reaching over 2000 score by destroying a large grey player.
Animated channel intro logo.
Kwebbelkop spawns as a red block, collects stray blocks to form 2x2 and 3x3 squares, and explains the game.
Static joke image of a keyboard in front of a microwave.
Player collects blocks, kills smaller players (Flash B, ZephPlayz, fake kwebbelkop), and explains how movement speed scales with main block size.
Static joke image of a Nokia 3310 mobile phone.
Player reaches #1 on the leaderboard while roaming near other players.
Static joke image of a Nokia 3310 mobile phone.
Player moves along the right border wall, demonstrates outer blocks exploding on white obstacles, and loses a large secondary block to a trap on a white obstacle.
Player shoots blocks with W to keep his named core block small and fast while building massive secondary blocks, killing multiple players including #2 to exceed 2200 score.
Player's largest secondary block shatters on a white obstacle; player then intentionally shoots away blocks with W and runs into white obstacles to feed mass to fans until dying.
Player shows the December 14th patch notes on the title screen, signs off, and plays an outro card.
Brief flash of main menu followed by Gaming Felix animated channel intro.
Player enters nickname GamingFelix, clicks Play Game, and views the rotating 3x3 gem cube loading screen.
Player spawns as a green block, collects stray blocks, tests shooting a block with W, and dies after touching a white obstacle block.
Game Over screen shows score 35; player clicks Continue and watches the rotating cube loading animation.
Player spawns as a yellow block, scavenges stray blocks, tests rotation, climbs to #2 on the leaderboard with over 650 score, and dies fighting cyan player ptm1023.
Game Over screen displays score 257 while player gives outro commentary.
Kwebbelkop showcases the mobile app menu, Game Modes selector (Free For All, Teams), Daily/Weekly/All Time leaderboards, and updated web menu.
Player plays with the Kwebbelkop skin on the dark grid background, demonstrating the central Heart Block, smashing large neutral food gem blocks, and shedding 1x1 blocks while spinning.
Player joins the same server on his mobile phone as KOPS alongside his PC character Kwebbelkop, battles Abril and Kylsifer to reach #1, and suicides his mobile character into his PC character.
Player battles Kylsifer, explains score decay at large sizes, and intentionally lets red player dahu destroy his exposed Heart Block.
Game Over screen shows score 1316 and Highest Position #1, followed by mobile app promotion and outro card.
Player opens the Skin selector, cycles through YouTuber and color skins to select the yellow MasterOv M skin, and starts a game.
Player uses the MasterOv skin, kills several players (Alex, messyourself, Poland, Coolio) to reach #2 with 1109 score, and dies when his main block clips a white obstacle.
Game Over screen shows score 1109 and Highest Position #2; player clicks Continue.
Player spawns, is quickly cornered and killed by giant red player sweden, and clicks Continue on the Game Over screen.
Player builds a large MasterOv block, destroys blocky wocky, don't kill, KOPS, and weedle to reach #2, then dies colliding with #1 CiaranPixelz.
Game Over screen shows score 827 and Highest Position #2 as player concludes the video.
Brief highlight clip of KOPS killing a yellow player followed by channel intro animation.
Player KOPS uses the Kwebbelkop skin, destroys several players including CiaranPixelz to exceed 1300 score, and is killed by #1 [MG] Exploi.
Player respawns on a new server, kills multiple players including jelly fan and alan to reach #1 with >1350 score, until a network instability popup disconnects the game.
Player selects the green Jelly skin, spawns as Jelly, kills KOPS and KO to reach #2, and gets disconnected by a network instability popup.
Player opens the server region dropdown and dark background toggle, selects the red Slogoman skin, battles to #1 with 777 score, and is disconnected by a network popup.
Facecam commentary and channel end-card.

Player [GD] plays on the dark background, carefully aligning stray blocks row by row and using a white obstacle to trim a protruding block until forming a single seamless 121-score square gem, before disconnecting.
Brief meme clip followed by streamer outro over the early dark-themed Blockor.io title screen.
Player Jelly spawns as a yellow block, explains basic mechanics, and dies colliding with an orange player (Score: 57).
Player spawns as a red block, steals blocks from LatvianGamer, kills Evielolstar and dy1xn to reach #1, observes joshplayuk's hollow ring build, and dies fighting SmAsHeR.
Game Over screen shows score 425 while player reacts and plays his channel outro.

rules.rule: A player spawns as a single 1x1 square gem block with their nickname displayed across their main/core block.
Touching small stray 1x1 blocks floating on the map attaches them to the player's block structure at the point of contact on a grid alignment.
When attached blocks form a complete solid square (e.g., 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, up to giant squares), they automatically merge into a single larger glossy gem block.
Players can build complex multi-block structures with multiple merged squares of varying sizes or hollow ring shapes attached to their core block.
In the later update (Feb 2017 / mobile release), the player's core block is represented by a specific 2x2-sized Heart Block marked with a heart icon, rather than the largest merged block.
The player's block cluster moves continuously toward the mouse cursor position on PC (or virtual directional arrow on mobile).
Pressing A rotates the player's block cluster counter-clockwise and pressing D rotates it clockwise.
Rotating with A or D consumes energy from the vertical green bar on the bottom-left and grants a temporary movement/rotational speed boost.
In the later update (Video D), rotating/spinning causes unmerged 1x1 outer blocks to detach and fall off the player's structure.
Pressing W shoots/ejects a 1x1 block from the player's structure toward the cursor, which also consumes a small amount of the green energy bar.
In the initial version (Videos A, B, C, E, F, H), shooting blocks with W can break down the player's own main block into smaller blocks to regain high movement speed.
Movement speed decreases as the player's main block / total mass grows larger.
The camera is top-down 2D, centered on the player's core block, and dynamically zooms out as the player's block structure grows larger.
When two players collide, larger blocks destroy smaller blocks on contact, shattering them into collectible 1x1 blocks.
In the initial version, a player dies immediately if their main (named) block is destroyed by a larger enemy block; losing outer/secondary blocks does not kill the player.
In the later Heart Block update (Video D), a player dies if and only if their Heart Block is destroyed.
White/grey square obstacle blocks are scattered throughout the arena and form a continuous perimeter wall around the map.

If a player's outer/secondary block touches a white obstacle block, that block explodes/shatters into small 1x1 blocks; if the player's main/core block touches a white obstacle block in the early version, the player dies or their main block shatters.
If a white obstacle block is hit enough times, it is destroyed and disappears from the map.

In the later update (Video D), large neutral colored gem blocks ('food blocks') spawn around the map; players with sufficiently large blocks can ram them to shatter them into a cluster of collectible 1x1 blocks.
Each 1x1 block attached to the player's structure equals 1 point of score, which is tracked in real time on the leaderboard.
In the later update (Video D), large players experience slow score decay (losing approximately 1 block per second) to prevent passive camping.

The HUD displays a 4-quadrant minimap in the top-left showing player dots, a vertical green energy/power bar (0 to 100) in the bottom-left, and a Top 10 leaderboard plus the player's current rank and score in the top-right.

Players can select free cosmetic skins (solid colors or YouTuber/creator logos such as Kwebbelkop, MasterOv, Jelly, Slogoman, AzzyLand, FaZe Mojo) from the Skin menu, which apply to every merged square block in their structure.
The settings menu allows players to toggle a Dark Background theme and select a server region (Europe Frankfurt/London, N. America East/Central/West/South, Asia Tokyo/Singapore).
The game supports cross-platform multiplayer between web browsers (PC) and mobile devices (iOS/Android), as well as Party codes (Create/Join) and Free For All / Teams modes.
In the later update (Video D), popping/collecting sound effects play when picking up small blocks or shattering large blocks.

areas.name: Main Menu / Title Screen
areas.description: Purple background with floating 3D gem blocks, featuring the BLOCKOR.IO logo, nickname input field, Play Game button, Skin selector button, Game Modes button (Free For All / Teams), settings gear dropdown (server region selector and Dark Background toggle), Party Create/Join buttons, changelog notes, and links to Leaderboards/Privacy Policy.

areas.name: Skin Selector Screen
areas.description: Overlay screen over the grid background with left and right arrows to preview and save block skins (solid gem colors and YouTuber/influencer logos) before entering a match.

areas.name: Main Arena (Light Theme)
areas.description: A large square 2D arena with a white/light-grey diamond-patterned background, bounded on all four sides by a wall of white/grey obstacle blocks and populated with scattered obstacle blocks and colorful 1x1 collectible blocks.

areas.name: Main Arena (Dark Theme)
areas.description: The same square 2D arena rendered with a dark grey/black diamond-patterned background for high contrast with bright gem blocks and glowing food blocks.

feel.core_loop: Spawn as a single 1x1 block, roam the arena collecting stray 1x1 blocks so they snap onto your grid and merge into larger glossy square gems, use A/D to rotate and W to shed/shoot blocks for speed or symmetry, avoid white obstacle blocks that shatter your structure, and ram smaller players' core/heart blocks to shatter and absorb their mass while climbing to #1 on the leaderboard.
feel.why_players_loved_it: Players loved the satisfying spatial puzzle of aligning 1x1 blocks into massive, gleaming gem squares (or 'perfect pearls'), the custom YouTuber skins that tiled across every square in their cluster, the high-stakes risk/reward of spinning and squeezing between deadly white obstacle blocks, and the ability to outmaneuver bigger players by shedding mass to stay fast or exposing/protecting a specific core/heart block.
feel.moment_to_moment: Fast and nimble when small, transitioning into a heavy, deliberate juggernaut as your central square grows. Combat is tense and positional—players constantly rotate their clusters to bring their largest merged blocks to bear against an opponent's vulnerable core or heart block while watching their rotation energy bar and dodging mines.
feel.together: Players competed in real-time Free For All and Team arenas across PC and mobile, hunted down the #1 leaderboard holder in packs, used Party links to join friends' servers, and frequently teamed up or fed blocks to favorite streamers by shooting blocks with W or intentionally shattering themselves on white obstacles.

unknowns: Exact mathematical formula governing movement speed reduction relative to main block size vs. total block count across different patches.
Exact regeneration rate and consumption cost per degree of rotation or per W-shot for the bottom-left green energy bar.
Exact rules and team mechanics of the 'Teams' game mode shown in the mobile menu dropdown in Video D (00:16).
Exact contents and pricing of 'Blockor Plus' and the in-game Store mentioned in Video D (00:21, 04:40).
